12109.quietTitle: Under Fla. Stat. §95.192, continuous ownership and tax payment for 4+ years after the deed often supports marketable title without suit. For faster insurable title, a quiet title action with final judgment is standard practice.

48041.notes: Redeemable tax deed (Texas Tax Code Ch. 34). Brazos County tax foreclosure sales are conducted by the Sheriff/constable process on the first Tuesday of each month when judgments are set (in-person; historically advertised via Bid4Assets notices and local counsel). Lists via Perdue Brandon / LGBS-style tax-sale firms when active. Obtain statement of no delinquent taxes before deed issues (§34.015). Sold without warranty subject to statutory redemption.

auctionPlatform.label: Brazos County Sheriff / Tax Office — Tax Foreclosure Sale (first Tuesday)

48041.auctionFrequency: First Tuesday of each month when sales are scheduled (10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. legal hours)
48041.depositRules: Typically no platform deposit — appear with capacity for cash/cashier's check for full purchase same day. Obtain written statement of no delinquent taxes from Brazos County Tax Assessor-Collector ($10 fee process under §34.015; allow processing time before sale). Post-judgment taxes may be due beyond minimum bid. Confirm exact payment payee and cutoff with Sheriff Civil / Tax Office before sale day.

taxCollector.label: Brazos County Tax Assessor-Collector

48041.survivingLiens: HOA/POA liens can survive a Texas tax sale if the association recorded its lien and was not properly joined/notified in the foreclosure suit. Federal tax liens survive (IRS rights). Post-judgment taxes and unjoined municipal liens may remain — search deed records and the appraisal district before bidding. Sheriff/constable deed is without warranty.
48041.quietTitle: Not legally mandatory, but title companies generally require a completed suit to quiet title before insuring, because of statutory redemption rights (homestead/ag up to 2 years; others ~180 days) and possible un-joined lienholders.
